identity.description: Decomposes a series into named latent states — level, trend, seasonal, cycle, AR — each an explicit stochastic component in one linear-Gaussian state space. The product is the interpretable decomposition itself (each state is a nameable curve), fitted by Kalman filtering/smoothing with exact missing-data handling.

consumes.note: regular time index required; NaN values handled exactly by the underlying Kalman machinery
optional exogenous regressors (intervention/holiday effects) aligned to the series index

emits.note: the named component states — level, trend, seasonal, cycle — as smoothed (and filtered) series with Gaussian uncertainty; the decomposition IS the output
component variance parameters + exog coefficients with SEs — which components carry the variation

level.note: trend specification — local level vs local linear trend vs random walk with drift vs smooth trend

seasonal.note: seasonal period; null omits the seasonal state entirely

cycle.note: stochastic cycle component for non-seasonal periodicity

autoregressive.note: AR state order for short-run dynamics the named components miss

invariances.why: linear-Gaussian components rescale equivariantly with the series; the decomposition is isomorphic under rescaling
the components are ADDITIVE — a log transform is precisely the multiplicative-vs-additive decomposition choice, not a no-op
same Kalman machinery as the DLM — missing observations skip the measurement update exactly, and the components interpolate through the gap with honest widening
numeric series; interventions/holidays enter as numeric exog design columns
assumes the series is an additive sum of linear-Gaussian components with mutually independent innovations
the seasonal state needs multiple full cycles to be identifiable; level-only specs remain usable on short series
forecasts propagate each component's state forward — trend continues, seasonal repeats — with widening intervals

featureStats.why: lag-k autocorrelation says whether a seasonal state is warranted at all; forcing one onto a non-seasonal series adds unidentified variance parameters
the seasonal state's identifiability requires multiple complete cycles — too few is a gate to a level/trend-only spec
exact in-filter gap handling is the family advantage — high missingness favors this over interpolate-then-decompose (STL)

modelMetrics.why: the component-selection lens: each added stochastic component must earn its variance parameter in penalized likelihood, not just absorb residual
a component whose innovation variance estimates near zero is deterministic or absent — the parsimony signal to drop it from the spec
whitened one-step innovations mean the named components captured the structure; autocorrelation left over says the spec is incomplete

edgeCases.condition: seasonal spec with < 2 full cycles of history
component variance estimated at the zero boundary
edgeCases.behavior: component collapses to deterministic; boundary SEs invalid

edgeCases.condition: smoothed component states used as as-of features

driver.constructor: UnobservedComponents(endog, level='llevel'|'lltrend', seasonal=s, cycle=..., autoregressive=..., exog=...).fit() then .smooth()
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter (time_col, value_col, freq — NaN preserved); expose each component (level/trend/seasonal/cycle) as a NAMED latent-state channel, filtered and smoothed separately for the as-of discipline

canBeSeeds.via: latent-state -> series adapter (seasonally-adjusted series = observed minus seasonal state, feeding a downstream forecaster)

placementClaims.why: the filter handles gaps exactly and attributes them honest uncertainty; pre-imputation injects fabricated observations the decomposition then treats as real
a log transform converts multiplicative seasonality to the additive form the component sum assumes
scale-equivariant; the decomposition rescales with the series
numeric series; intervention dummies are modeling-side exog, not a preprocessing stage
